editor.data.airQuality.airnowTerms: {lead} AirNow’s data-use guidelines bind whoever shows this data: credit the reporting agency first, then AirNow — the {attribution} column does it; mark observations as preliminary — the {preliminary} column says which rows are; never alter the numbers, forecasts or advisory text; show only current data — the expiry below blanks readings that stop updating; and let the agencies know you are using it. That last one is yours to do. {link}
editor.data.airQuality.areaHint: The area id is the number in the reporting area’s EnviroFlash feed address — {example} is Phoenix, so its id is {id}.
editor.data.airQuality.columnsHint: Every provider returns the same columns — {columns} and the rest — so switching from AirNow to CAMS does not mean rebuilding the graphic.
editor.data.cap.columnsHint: One row per alert, most severe first — {columns} and the rest. Test messages, cancellations and alerts past their expiry are always dropped.
editor.data.cap.localDayHint: Alerts are read as whole calendar days in this zone, ignoring the offsets the feed prints. Use it for AirNow action days, whose offsets are wrong for half the year.
editor.data.cap.sourcesHint: Any CAP alert, CAP-in-Atom feed or NWS alerts GeoJSON. NWS for a state: {nws}. AirNow action days and alerts: {airnow}.
editor.data.credentialFtp: Credential id (optional — password or SSH key, held server-side)
editor.data.credentialOther: Credential id (optional — the value lives in server config)
editor.data.credentialSheets: Credential id (required — API key or service-account JSON, held server-side)
editor.data.emptyHint: No data sources. A published Google Sheet works as an {httpCsv} source — use its {publish} URL, no API key needed.
editor.data.expireAfter: Blank the rows after (hours without a successful fetch)
editor.data.expireAfterHint: Leave empty to keep showing the last good data for ever, as other sources do. Set it for data that must not be shown stale: the rows empty — the columns stay — and come back with the next successful fetch.
editor.data.expired: Expired — no successful fetch within its limit, so the rows are blank until the next one.
editor.data.ftp.allowHostsHint: A drop box on the venue LAN is refused until its host is allowlisted — add it to {env} in the server environment. The file is parsed by the same readers the HTTP sources use, so the same CSV over SFTP and over HTTPS gives the same table.
editor.data.ftp.plainWarning: Plain FTP sends the password and the file in the clear. Fine for an anonymous public drop; use SFTP or FTPS for anything with a login.
editor.data.guard.backupHint: The backup’s rows go on air under this source’s id, so bound tables and tickers need no change — give it the same columns. A manual table with one “temporarily unavailable” row makes a good last resort.
editor.data.guard.badRowsDrop: Is left out; the rest go on air
editor.data.guard.fallbackOnExpired: When this has nothing to show
editor.data.guard.fallbackOnFailing: As soon as a fetch fails
editor.data.guard.hint: A fetch that fails these checks is treated like one that failed to connect: the last good rows stay on air and the status says why.
editor.data.guard.maxDropTitle: Refuse a fetch that loses more than this share of the rows at once. A drop that holds for three fetches in a row is believed.
editor.data.guard.maxUnchangedTitle: A feed answering with the same rows for this long is treated as expired — blank, or its backup. For feeds that should keep changing: observations, a sheet a script updates.
editor.data.guard.previewDropped: {count, plural, one {The guard would leave out # row.} other {The guard would leave out # rows.}}
editor.data.guard.previewRefused: The guard would refuse this fetch: {reason}
editor.data.guard.stuck: Frozen — the content has not changed within its limit, so it is treated as expired.
editor.data.guard.title: When the data is bad
editor.data.guard.useTitle: Whose rows go on air. Automatic follows the rules; the other two are an operator override, until changed or the server restarts.
editor.data.manual.bracketHint: Type a winner or a score and the rounds after it fill themselves. Filled slots are locked — the table layer's own {advance} owns them.
editor.data.manual.fedCell: Filled by the bracket — edit the round before it
editor.data.manual.pasteHint: Paste a block from a spreadsheet into the first cell to replace the whole table, headers included.
editor.data.media.columnsHint: Point a media cell at mediaSrc and add a Filter on mediaOk equals true: a camera that is down or frozen drops out of the rotation.
editor.data.media.frozenAfterTitle: Seconds of the same picture before a camera counts as frozen. 0 switches it off.
editor.data.media.hint: For a list of cameras or streams: the server checks each row’s URL and adds mediaState, mediaOk, mediaSrc and mediaKind to every row.

editor.data.sheets.preferCsvHint: For a sheet you can publish, {httpCsv} is simpler and needs no credential. Use this type when the sheet must stay private — then share it with the service account's {email}, or use an API key if it is link-shared.

editor.data.weather.allowHostsHint: A private or loopback address is refused by the fetch guard until it is allowlisted — set {env} in the server environment.
editor.data.weather.attribution: {lead} Show “{credit}” wherever this data appears — bind a text layer to the {column} column and it travels with the graphic. {link}
editor.data.weather.columnsHint: Every provider returns the same columns — {columns} and the rest — so switching provider does not mean rebuilding the graphic. {icon} is a fixed keyword such as {example}, to map onto your own artwork.
editor.data.weather.contact: Contact for User-Agent (optional — overrides the server default)
editor.data.weather.contactOptional: Not required here, but it identifies your station in the origin’s logs. Set it once for the whole server with {env} rather than per source.
editor.data.weather.contactRequired: {provider} requires this and will contact you before blocking if a problem is traced to your requests. Left blank, Breeze sends a generic string shared by every install — so your traffic is judged alongside everyone else’s and nobody can reach you. Set it once for the whole server with {env} instead of per source.
editor.data.weather.coverageHint: Coverage: {coverage}. Polls no faster than every {seconds}s.
editor.data.weather.modelDocsHint: Not sure of the model id? {link} let you pick a model and read the id straight off the generated URL — it is the same {param} value this field takes. Only the model and time zone are worth copying across; the rest of the URL is built for you.
editor.data.weather.nonCommercial: {lead} Open-Meteo’s hosted API may not be used on a channel or site carrying advertising or subscriptions. For commercial output, run your own Open-Meteo instance and pick {selfHosted}, or subscribe to their paid API. {link}.
editor.data.weather.observedHint: A measurement from the nearest station, not a forecast — {age} says how old it was when it arrived and {station} which station took it.
editor.data.weather.pairDayNight: One row per day — pair each day with the night after it
editor.data.weather.place: Place name (shown on the graphic, never sent to the provider)
editor.data.weather.syncedModelsHint: Your instance only holds the models you have synced. If it answers on {query} but not without, name that model here — leaving it blank asks for {fallback}, which may want a model the box does not have.
editor.data.xmlFeedHint: This is {feed, select, atom {an Atom} other {an RSS}} feed. The {rssType} source type will normalize it to stable columns — worth using instead unless you specifically want the raw element names.
editor.layers.flattened: Flattened to images, so they cannot be edited or bound:

editor.properties.advanceCarryTitle: Side-prefixed suffixes carried forward together, e.g. Team, Code.
editor.properties.advanceHint: A match with no winner advances nobody — an unplayed slot stays blank rather than guessing.
editor.properties.advanceLoserRoutesTitl: Where a loser goes — this is how a third-place play-off gets filled.
editor.properties.advanceOrderWarning: {advance} needs every round in the data. Anything that drops rows before it — filter, limit, offset — leaves it nothing to advance from. Move it to the top.
editor.properties.advanceRoutesTitle: Optional per-row routing, e.g. QFL-1:home. Blank rows use the implied tree.

editor.properties.bindingCrawlTitle: Operators can replace the whole item list live; the new copy is swapped in at the loop seam
editor.properties.bindingTableTitle: Operators can replace the whole table live from the control panel
editor.properties.bindingTextTitle: Operators can update this field live
editor.properties.cellClockHint: Drawn once per data row. Keyframe times are measured from the row's arrival, not the composition's start, so a cell rides its row's reveal stagger.
editor.properties.channelTitle: The name an operator triggers: /api/control/<project>/<channel>/play. Defaults to the referenced composition's id.
editor.properties.clockBindingClash: This layer also has a binding. A clock always wins, so the operator field would do nothing — clear one or the other.
editor.properties.clockLanguageHint: Month and weekday names on air. A property of this graphic, not of the editor — the preview above shows exactly what will render.
editor.properties.clockPlaceholderNote: Content above is a placeholder — the canvas and a still export use it, a renderer never does.
editor.properties.crawlColumnHint: Items come from {column}, refreshed whenever the source changes. Empty cells are skipped, and if the column comes back empty the typed items stay up.
editor.properties.crawlNoColumn: Pick a column — until one is set the ticker keeps using its typed items.
editor.properties.crawlNoSource: No data source with id {id} in this project. The ticker falls back to its typed items.
editor.properties.cycleDwellTitle: Turn pages on a timer while the graphic holds. 0 switches cycling off and keeps the settings below
editor.properties.cycleEndContinue: Continue — on to the next STOP or the outro
editor.properties.cycleGroupTitle: Tables with the same group turn together and hold together
editor.properties.cycleKeyColumnTitle: The column whose value on a page's first row names the page — what the control panel and Companion show, and what page?name= looks for

editor.properties.followColumnTitle: The column in this table that must equal the leader's page key
editor.properties.followLeaderColumnTitl: The leader's column that names its page. Blank uses the leader's cycle key column, then the match column
editor.properties.followReadout: Each time {table} turns, this table shows only the rows whose {column} matches its page. No match shows no rows.
editor.properties.followTableTitle: The table whose page this one follows: its binding, mount.binding, or layer id. The nearest match wins where a graphic is mounted more than once
editor.properties.formatTitle: Tokens: HH H hh h mm m ss s A a · DD D MMMM MMM MM M · dddd ddd YYYY YY · [literal]
editor.properties.independentTitle: Give this element its own timeline and its own PLAY, triggered separately from everything else on the page

editor.properties.mediaBindingTitle: A field on the control panel — the operator can type a URL to play
editor.properties.mediaCellHint: In a table with one row a page and a cycle, this is a camera rotation. Skip needs the cycle.
editor.properties.mediaHint: Live media plays whatever is live when it is shown; it does not follow the timeline.
editor.properties.mediaRefreshTitle: For snapshots: seconds between fetching a new picture
editor.properties.name: Name
editor.properties.noAlphaHint: This format cannot carry an alpha channel in a browser source. Transcode it in the asset bin if it needs transparency.

editor.properties.overrideSetTitle: Override this field for this mount only

editor.properties.resortTitle: Seconds rows take to slide to a new order when the data re-sorts. 0 snaps.

editor.properties.rulePreviewModeTitle: How the stage shows the graphic in a mode. The editor’s own setting: it does not change the mode on air.
editor.properties.ruleSrcTitle: The image while this rule holds. {column} is filled from the row the rule reads.
editor.properties.ruleWhereTitle: Optional. Which row to read — the first whose column equals the value, e.g. place=Phoenix. Blank reads the first row.
editor.properties.rulesCellHint: In a table, a rule can read this cell’s own row — the reading turns orange on the row that is over 100. Rules apply in order; a later one wins.
editor.properties.rulesHint: Show, hide or recolour this layer — or change its image — from data, a field, or the channel’s mode. Rules apply in order; a later one wins. A layer with a “show” rule is hidden until one holds.
editor.properties.selectALayer: Select a layer to edit its properties.
editor.properties.separatorCustomHint: Spaces are part of the value — pad either side of the glyph, or the items run together.
editor.properties.separatorCustomPlaceho: Spaces count — include the padding you want either side of the glyph
editor.properties.separatorPreviewHint: Renders as “A{sep}B{sep}”, wrapping round to the first item.
editor.properties.separatorTitle: Printed between items, and again between the last and the first
editor.properties.speedTitle: Pixels per second, independent of the composition's duration
editor.properties.spriteNoBinding: A multi-frame sheet cannot be bound — the incoming sheet would be stepped through this one’s grid.
editor.properties.spriteTiming: {frames} frames at {fps}fps — {seconds}s. Independent of the layer’s in/out points.
editor.properties.staggerTitle: Seconds between consecutive pieces. 0 animates them together.
editor.properties.stingerHint: A stinger usually wants Clear — a held final frame stays over the program feed once the transition is done.
editor.properties.tableNoColumns: No columns yet — attach a source or paste rows into a manual table.
editor.properties.tableNoSource: No data source with id {id} in this project. The table falls back to its authored rows.
editor.properties.tableOverflow: More rows than fit. NEXT pages through them while the graphic holds — add a STOP marker so it has somewhere to hold, or raise the layer height.
editor.properties.timezoneTitle: IANA zone, e.g. America/Phoenix. Blank uses the render machine's own zone.
editor.properties.timezoneUnknown: That time zone is not one this machine knows.
editor.properties.transformSourceMissing: No data source with id {id} in this project — this step adds nothing.

editor.properties.unfilledTitle: Draw the outline only — what a line or an underline wants

server.pages.activityEmpty: Nothing recorded yet. Projects and scenes created or deleted, and control panels connecting, are logged here.
server.pages.activityFooterAttribution: Breeze has no accounts, so an action is attributed to the address it came from and the browser it came from — not to a person. On a LAN with assigned machines that is usually enough to identify who; behind a proxy or a VPN it is not, and this page does not pretend otherwise.
server.pages.activityFooterStorage: Written to {path}, one JSON object per line, one file per month. Nothing deletes them for you. Browser sources are not recorded — the portal's status strip shows what is connected right now.
server.pages.allFedHint: Every field here is fed by a data source and updates on its own. There is nothing to send.
server.pages.apiKeyOffTitle: Anyone on the network can edit and control this server. Set BREEZE_API_KEY and restart to require a key.
server.pages.backupFooter: A bundle carries composition JSON, the asset index, referenced asset files and data-source definitions. It never carries the Breeze runtime, so it is inert without an install — and it never carries credentials. A restored data source keeps its secret {id} and loses its keys and tokens, so it will need them re-entered on the machine it lands on.

server.pages.peersFooterRefresh: This page refreshes every 5 seconds. A connection is identified by its address and browser only — Breeze has no accounts.
server.pages.peersMonitors: {count, plural, one {Plus # element readout opened by a scene panel, not listed separately.} other {Plus # element readouts opened by scene panels, not listed separately.}}
server.pages.peersNoneApi: {seconds, plural, one {No API calls in the last # second.} other {No API calls in the last # seconds.}}
server.pages.peersNonePanels: No control panels or editors open.
server.pages.peersPreviews: {count, plural, one {Plus # output preview embedded in a control panel.} other {Plus # output previews embedded in control panels.}}
server.pages.portalFooterClip: {lead} It renders 1:1 at the composition's full size — 1920×1080 for the demos — and a browser window is always shorter than that, so the bottom of the frame falls outside the window. A graphic low in the frame, like the news ticker at y=1000, plays correctly and is simply not on screen: it looks as though nothing happened when PLAY is pressed. Use the {debug} to watch it in a window, and the Output URL only in a source sized to the composition. The console on that page says so too.
server.pages.portalFooterClipLead: Opening an Output URL in a desktop browser will clip the frame.
server.pages.portalFooterKeys: Keys in a debug tab: {space} play · {nextKey} next · {esc} stop · {backspace} clear.
server.pages.portalFooterLinks: {control} drives a graphic on air — play, stop and live field edits. {output} is what you paste into a vMix Web Browser input or an OBS Browser Source: transparent, 1:1, no controls. {debug} scales the stage to the window and shows an FPS and playback overlay.
server.pages.previewDebugTitle: Toggle the debug overlay inside the preview
server.pages.previewHint: A real output page on this channel, scaled to fit. It follows what you trigger here, picks up from an output already on air when it opens, and is never counted as a connected output.
server.pages.previewSyncTitle: Which output the preview picks up from when it opens with the graphic already on air. It follows what you trigger here either way.
server.pages.projectKeyTitle: Project key {key} — it goes in every /play and /control URL, API call and Companion connection for this project. Click the icon to copy it.
server.pages.secondsAgo: {count, plural, one {# second ago} other {# seconds ago}}
server.pages.signInHint: Signs this browser in for twelve hours, so the editor can save and panels can control graphics. The browser keeps a session, never the key. A server restart signs everyone out.
server.pages.signOutHint: This browser can save in the editor and use the panels without the key in their address. Sign out on a shared machine.
server.pages.sourcesHint: AUTO lets the source’s own rules decide. OWN keeps its own rows on air even when they are stale or frozen — not once they have expired; BACKUP puts its backup on air. Either stays until changed or the server restarts.
server.pages.updateHint: Changes apply live — the graphic does not need re-playing. Fields marked {fed} come from a data source and update on their own.
